title: Database Change Data Capture
summary: Change data capture streams every committed change in a database to other systems without the application having to publish anything. A connector reads the database's own write-ahead log, the same log used for replication, and turns each insert, update, and delete into an ordered event. Search indexes, caches, and warehouses then stay in sync within seconds, and they can never miss a write the database actually committed.

walkthrough.title: Application commits
walkthrough.text: The app runs UPDATE orders SET status = 'shipped' WHERE id = 42 and commits. It does nothing else: no dual writes to Kafka or search.

walkthrough.title: Read the write-ahead log
walkthrough.text: The connector holds a logical replication slot. Postgres decodes the WAL record into a row change with before and after values, in commit order.

walkthrough.title: Register the schema
walkthrough.text: The connector registers the table's schema (Avro or Protobuf) with a schema registry, so consumers can decode events and the schema can evolve safely.

walkthrough.title: Publish keyed events
walkthrough.text: The change is published to topic db.public.orders keyed by primary key, so all changes to order 42 land in one partition and stay in order.

walkthrough.title: Sinks apply changes
walkthrough.text: Consumers upsert into Elasticsearch, invalidate cache keys, and load the warehouse. They apply events idempotently by key and log position, so redelivery is harmless.

walkthrough.title: Acknowledge the log position
walkthrough.text: After Kafka confirms the write, the connector reports the processed log sequence number (LSN) to the database, which can then discard WAL older than that.

walkthrough.title: Snapshot and resume
walkthrough.text: A new connector first takes a consistent snapshot of existing rows, then switches seamlessly to streaming the log from the snapshot's position.

data.label: Application
tech: Any service writing to the DB
responsibilities: Writes only to its database, the single source of truth.
Needs no knowledge of downstream consumers.
Uses transactions so related changes commit together.

failureModes.scenario: Dual writes (DB, then Kafka) instead of CDC
failureModes.impact: A crash between the two leaves systems inconsistent.
failureModes.mitigation: CDC or the transactional outbox pattern.

failureModes.impact: A flood of change events overwhelms sinks.
failureModes.mitigation: Batch large migrations; throttle; warn downstream teams.

data.label: Source Database

output.name: Change stream
output.type: Decoded row changes in commit order (LSN)

responsibilities: Records every change in its write-ahead log for durability.
Decodes log records into logical row changes for subscribers.
Keeps log segments until the slot confirms it has consumed them.

failureModes.impact: Unconsumed WAL piles up and fills the database disk.
failureModes.mitigation: Alert on slot lag; max_slot_wal_keep_size as a safety limit.

failureModes.impact: Replication slot may not exist on the new primary.
failureModes.mitigation: Failover-aware slots, or re-snapshot after failover.

data.label: CDC Connector

output.name: Events
output.type: { before, after, op: 'u', source: { lsn, ts } }

responsibilities: Turns log records into structured change events.
Snapshots existing data, then streams changes with no gap.
Records its position so restarts resume exactly.

failureModes.mitigation: Sinks apply idempotently using key and LSN.
Compatible migrations; schema registry compatibility rules.

data.label: Schema Registry
responsibilities: Rejects incompatible changes that would break consumers.
Lets each event carry a small schema ID instead of the full schema.

failureModes.scenario: Breaking change registered with compatibility off
failureModes.impact: Consumers fail to decode new events.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce BACKWARD or FULL compatibility per subject.

failureModes.impact: New schema versions cannot be used.
failureModes.mitigation: Clients cache schemas; run the registry highly available.

data.label: Change Topics

output.name: Ordered stream
output.type: Per-key ordered changes to all consumers

responsibilities: Keeps per-row ordering by partitioning on primary key.
Lets many sinks consume independently at their own pace.
Compacts to the latest value per key for bootstrapping new sinks.

failureModes.impact: Keys move partitions, so ordering breaks.
failureModes.mitigation: Choose partition counts up front; migrate with a new topic.

failureModes.impact: A new sink never learns a row was deleted.
failureModes.mitigation: Tombstone retention long enough for consumers.

data.label: Downstream Sinks
responsibilities: Keep derived copies in sync within seconds.
Apply events idempotently, ignoring older versions.
Rebuild from a snapshot plus the stream when needed.

failureModes.mitigation: Design per-entity views; tolerate eventual consistency.
Lag monitoring and scaling consumers per partition.
